sections.section_name: Section B - Art Elements & Conceptual Terms

questions.question_text: Explain the meaning and structural importance of 'Rupabheda' as the first core component within the Six Limbs of Indian Painting (Shadang). [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Rupabheda signifies the knowledge of appearance, form, and visual distinctions. It is structurally essential because it enables an artist to perceive, analyze, and render the unique physical proportions and traits that isolate one form from another.

questions.question_text: Define the aesthetic principle of 'Pramanam' as outlined in the Shadang, focusing on its role in creating structural compositions. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Pramanam dictates the correct perception of measure, proportion, and structural anatomy. It ensures that depicted subjects possess accurate physical scale and visual harmony within the broader artistic composition.

questions.question_text: Evaluate the role of 'Texture' as a core element of art in ancient Indus Valley terracotta sculptures like the Mother Goddess. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Texture provides tactile and visual depth. In terracottas, the rough, unglazed clay surface highlights structural crudeness and earthy authenticity, amplifying the primitive vigor of the fertility idol.

questions.question_text: Explain how the conceptual terms 'Bhava' and 'Lavanya Yojanam' complement each other to elevate an Indian classical painting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Bhava breathes emotional resonance and expressive life into a painting, while Lavanya Yojanam infuses grace and artistic beauty, ensuring the raw emotional expression remains visually captivating and harmonious.

questions.question_text: Identify and explain the specific application of 'Line' (Rekha) acting as a dominant element in the early cave murals of Ajanta. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Lines in Ajanta murals are rhythmic, lyrical, and incredibly fluid. They define character contours with varying thickness, creating three-dimensional volume and conveying delicate emotional expressions without requiring heavy shading.

questions.question_text: Deconstruct the stylistic modeling, posture dynamics, and aesthetic features of the famous polished sandstone 'Lion Capital of Sarnath' from the Mauryan Period. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The Sarnath Capital displays four highly stylized lions carved back-to-back sitting upon a cylindrical abacus. The abacus features low-relief carvings of a wheel, horse, bull, elephant, and lion separated by chakras. The surface shows an absolute mirror-like Mauryan polish, and the entire composition symbolizes the Dharmachakra pravartana, reflecting extreme structural symmetry and regal majesty.

questions.question_text: Analyze the aesthetic execution, postural attributes, and emotional resonance of the 'Padmapani Bodhisattva' mural located in Cave 1 of Ajanta. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The Padmapani Bodhisattva is a masterpiece of lyrical line work and subtle tonal variations. The figure exhibits the graceful 'tribhanga' (three-bends) posture while gently holding a blue lotus. The downward-looking, half-closed eyes convey immense compassion and spiritual tranquility. Subtle highlights on the nose and lips create a sweeping three-dimensional volume, seamlessly blending divine majesty with profound internal peace.

questions.question_text: Describe the core stylistic features, physical ornamentation, and construction technique of the 'Mother Goddess' terracotta figurine excavated from Mohenjo-daro. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Crafted using a basic pinching and appliqué technique, this unbaked clay figurine features a distinct fan-shaped headdress, prominent breasts, and a broad decorative collar. The crude, stylized form with pellet-like eyes completely lacks realistic anatomical proportions, aggressively emphasizing her symbolic status as a divine fertility deity.
